anchor_notes.reset: Ctrl+R is the emulator's hard reset. In GBP mode it fades the game (0.60 s) and stalls (1.58 s) before the boot: 2.175 s, included in every time below. Keep a copy of the ROM with no .sav beside it: gambatte auto-loads a .sav and NEW GAME silently becomes CONTINUE.

gse.focus_note: Same PC: play with a CONTROLLER and keep THIS terminal window focused, so ENTER reaches the tool while START and A reach the emulator. With keyboard controls one window would swallow the other's key: then run this tool on a second device next to you (a laptop or phone; the anchor is only your ENTER). The reset anchor (Ctrl+R is a keyboard hotkey to the emulator window) needs the second device, or a controller button bound to the hard reset.

psr-64c2.name: PSR Red/Blue Any% route: 'Manip TID 64C2 (25794)', the one published target
psr-64c2.route: the Trainer ID bytes become wCurMapScriptPtr in bank $16 after the save corruption; the route's swap list is written for 64C2 and no other value
psr-64c2.provenance: EMPIRICAL: the PSR route README (pokemon-speedrunning routes docs/gen-1/red-blue/main-any/README.md, 2026-09-02) names exactly one target, 'Manip TID 64C2 (25794)', with its swap list. $64C2 occurs in NO table under the hold-START methodologies (Red, Blue; offsets 0-5999), so a runner of that route should not expect this tool to reach it; the other bank-$16 values prior searches accepted are the separate, opt-in set bank16-family-inferred.

bank16-family-inferred.name: bank-$16 family {$64BD, $64BE, $64C1, $64C6} that the owner's prior route searches accepted (INFERRED: no published swap list)
bank16-family-inferred.route: INFERRED: each of these lands wCurMapScriptPtr in the same bank-$16 region as 64C2, but the PSR swap list is for 64C2 only; a member needs its own item-swap list, which nobody has published
bank16-family-inferred.provenance: INFERRED from ~/AI/speedrun-research/RESEARCH.md round-4 section 5.6 (the bank-$16 destinations prior searches accepted). Not route-valid for the PSR route as written: applying the 64C2 swap list to a 64BD save is not known to work. Red tables: $64BD at GBA offset 1084 and DMG offset 721 (one derivation each); no member in Blue's tables (offsets 0-5999).

hi40-corruption.name: $40xx high byte (owner's Red / Blue Any% save-corruption variant): any Trainer ID $4000-$40FF
hi40-corruption.route: the corruption's second swap is an 11-byte offset-preserving copy that lands ($D358, the Trainer ID's HIGH byte) in wCurMapScriptPtr with bank $1D mapped, so the jump target is $HH01 and $1D:$4001 is inside the map-block data that runs as a sled into HallOfFamePC at $1D:$405C. Swap 1 (party slots 7<->21) overwrites $D35A-$D364 and destroys the Trainer ID's LOW byte before swap 2 runs, so only the high byte reaches the pointer: every $4000-$40FF is route-valid, 1 in 256, and no $40xx is a trap
hi40-corruption.provenance: EMPIRICAL (emulator, 2026-09-04, Red): all 256 Trainer IDs $4000-$40FF, each driven through the documented 15-step button sequence with no forced PC and no poked menu variables, reach HallOfFamePC on frame 1472 with HL = $4001 at the 'jp hl' in RunMapScript; the Trainer ID read back after swap 1 is $4000 on every row. Isolation control on the same state: forcing $D358 to $AD gives jump $40AD and a hard lock, while Trainer ID $40AD reaches the Hall of Fame. Reproduced on a third corrupted save minted by gambatte-core from a genuine NEW GAME plus mid-save reset; an exhaustive search over all 65,280 swap index pairs finds no 1- or 2-swap path from $D35A to $D36E/$D36F. WITHDRAWN 2026-09-04: the earlier low-byte window $00-$38 / $3A-$5C (and its $39 hole) came from sweeps that poison the Trainer ID and poke wCurMapScriptPtr directly - column 5 of sled_blue_40.csv is the pointer low byte, not a Trainer ID low byte - so it constrains the JUMP POINTER and still governs the separate TID-free route, not this one. UNCONFIRMED ON HARDWARE: every measurement here is emulator work (PyBoy for the runs, gambatte-core for the saves and the hold tables); the claim is WRAM arithmetic rather than timing, so it should transfer, but no cartridge run has been done. INFERRED for Blue: $1D:$4000-$405B is byte-identical in pokeblue.gbc and the swap code is the same source, but no Blue corruption-route sweep was run. STRUCTURAL: pret/pokered bank $1D map-block data before HallOfFamePC.

psr-yellow.name: PSR Yellow Any% route: 'Manip TID 6415 (25621) or 64EA (25834)'
psr-yellow.route: 64EA saves 16 frames later in the run but is harder to hit; the item swap differs (TM34 -> Carbos instead of Boulderbadge -> Carbos)
psr-yellow.provenance: EMPIRICAL: the PSR route README (docs/gen-1/yellow/main-any/README.md, 2026-09-02): 'Manip TID: 6415 (25621) or 64EA (25834); this manip saves 16 frames later into the run, but it's harder to pull off'. Under yellow/*/hold-start-v1 neither ID occurs in offsets 0-5999 on either boot; 64EA occurs only under an after-intro hold on the DMG (START held from frames 2093-2305, menu 2360, offset 2005), not shipped as a methodology; 6415 was not found under any of the three Yellow plateaus swept (docs/FACTS.md).

red/gba/hold-start-v1.status: ACTIVE. Emulator-exact on GSE / gambatte-speedrun (GBP mode, GBC BIOS); hardware-validated on the GBA HD 5 of 5; GBA / GBA SP are the same silicon, not separately sampled; GameCube Game Boy Player UNVALIDATED (transfer test pending).
red/gba/hold-start-v1.predicts: the Trainer ID (Gen 1 has no Secret ID)
red/gba/hold-start-v1.protocol: Clear the save so the menu shows NEW GAME with no CONTINUE. Power on or hard reset, then touch nothing. Between 21.77 s and 24.70 s after the boot starts (frames 1300-1475) press START and keep it held; the intro's full-white flash at the end of the Nidorino/Gengar scene sits inside this window, so holding START as the screen flashes white is safe. The NEW GAME menu opens on frame 1553 (26.00 s) no matter where in the window START went down. The A press on NEW GAME is the one timed press: A frame = menu frame + 80 + offset, and the offset indexes the table. Read the Trainer ID off a Pokemon's status screen afterwards.
red/gba/hold-start-v1.landmark: the intro's full-white flash happens inside this window, so holding START as the screen flashes white is safe
validity: Pokemon Red (English) booted on GBA silicon with the GBC boot ROM: a GBA, GBA SP, GBA HD, GameCube Game Boy Player, or GSE / gambatte-speedrun in GBP mode with the GBC BIOS.
The save is cleared: the menu shows NEW GAME with no CONTINUE option.
Power on or hard reset, then no input at all before START.
START goes down inside frames 1300-1475 after the boot starts (21.77-24.70 s) and stays held until the NEW GAME menu opens.
The NEW GAME menu opens on frame 1553 (26.00 s); nothing is pressed between the menu opening and A.
One press of A on NEW GAME, and that press is the only timed input: A frame = 1553 + 80 + offset.

Any other input pattern (START before frame 1300 or after 1475, START tapped instead of held, any extra press, a CONTINUE menu) gives a different deterministic result that this methodology does not cover.
